title: "UI seems to imply a runner is running multiple tasks at once This shouldn't be the case as a runner should only do one task at a time.so double check this isn't the case and fix any issues that cause this.  The main worry is this dev box has limited memory and can crash if it does too much so we need to avoid that. # Goal
# UI seems to imply a runner is running multiple tasks at once

This shouldn't be the case as a runner should only do one task at a time.so double check this isn't the case and fix any issues that cause this. 

The main worry is this dev box has limited memory and can crash if it does too much so we need to avoid that. So one task per Runner at a time 

![18846.png](assets/18846.png)

And it should be very clear of this in the ui

Status: plan only — no code changed.\n6|\n7|## Step 0 verdict (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n8|\n9|Screenshot `assets/18846.png` is still absent from this task folder (only\n10|`SURVEY.md` + this plan exist). Hypothesis **(a) real double-hold is PROVEN**:\n11|a throwaway probe (`/tmp/kb-step1-probe.mjs`, not committed) claimed task-A\n12|and task-B as one `runnerId` and both holds are live; the existing\n13|`api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js` flow shows the dispatch path doing the\n14|same (runner `caps-1` direct-claims task A, then dispatch assigns it task B).\n15|The suspect widget is `PerRunnerTasksWidget` (one card per assignment, no\n16|per-runner grouping), so two holds for one `runnerId` render as two live\n17|\"Runner X\" cards — the reported look. `TaskCard` likewise badges every held\n18|task `RUNNING · <runnerId>`. Hypothesis (b) stale `running_*` labels remains\n19|possible as a secondary contributor; the backend fence + grouped UI below fix\n20|(a) and display-harden (b).\n21|\n22|## Goal\n23|\n24|Guarantee that one Runner executes at most one task at a time (protecting a\n25|memory-limited dev box from concurrent-work crashes), prove the guarantee with\n26|tests, and make the single-active-task state unmistakable in the UI.\n27|\n28|## Success Criteria\n29|\n30|1. A single `runnerId` can hold at most one live backend claim at any moment;\n31|   a second claim/dispatch attempt while one is live is refused loudly\n32|   (named error code, no silent queueing inside the Runner).\n33|2. The Runner daemon cannot start a second assignment while one is in flight,\n34|   even with a stale/retried dispatch answer.\n35|3. Every UI surface derives \"running\" from one source of truth, so two tasks\n36|   can never both render as running; stale `running_*` labels render as\n37|   stale/interrupted, never as live.\n38|4. Each Runner view shows exactly one \"current task\" slot plus an explicit\n39|   Busy/Free state (and, where cheap, queued-next and memory pressure).\n40|5. `npm run test:unit` passes; new regression tests cover the per-runner fence\n41|   and the UI single-active rendering.\n42|\n43|## Context and evidence (what research found)\n44|\n45|- Embedded engine already claims single-active execution: `ExecutionQueue`\n46|  serializes jobs (`api/flow/executionQueue.js`), and\n47|  `api/flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js` characterizes \"at most one live\n48|  running_* status\".\n49|- Frontend already has the right seam: `frontend/src/components/tasks/runningTask.js`\n50|  (`resolveRunningTask`, `isTaskRunning`, `isStaleRunner`) documents the\n51|  engine-owner lock and the \"phantom-second-runner\" bug class. Open question\n52|  is whether *all* surfaces use it (audit needed).\n53|- Fleet path has the gap: `ClaimStore.claim(taskId, runnerId, …)`\n54|  (`api/flow/claimStore.js`) enforces one holder per *task*, and dispatch\n55|  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, ~L993-1060) enforces a *fleet* cap and a\n56|  *per-project* cap — but nothing enforces one live hold per *runner*.\n57|  `countLiveHolds()` supports only a `projectId` filter; there is no\n58|  by-runner lookup. Two daemon processes sharing one `runnerId`/credential\n59|  (or a claim-route call racing a dispatch lease) can therefore hand one\n60|  Runner two live assignments on a small box.\n61|- Runner daemon loop (`runner/daemon.js`, `runDispatchLoop`) is sequentially\n62|  structured (poll → execute → poll), but there is no in-process\n63|  \"assignment in flight\" guard asserted around `executeAssignment`, and no\n64|  defense against a second process with the same identity.\n65|- Per-task live-claim UI exists: `RunnerBanner.jsx` renders from `task.claim`.\n66|  If two tasks ever carry claims for the same `runnerId` (see gap above), the\n67|  UI truthfully shows the forbidden state — the screenshot's \"one Runner, many\n68|  tasks\" look. Stale `running_*` labels are the second suspect (display-only).\n69|- Evidence gaps: the screenshot (`assets/18846.png`) is NOT present in this\n70|  task's docs folder (only `SURVEY.md` exists), and `SURVEY.md` has\n71|  `\"answers\": {}` (all questions unanswered). The plan below treats the survey\n72|  as open decisions with recommended defaults (§1), and Step 0 re-captures the\n73|  screenshot evidence.\n74|\n75|## How the survey shapes this plan (SURVEY.md, unanswered → advised defaults)\n76|\n77|| Survey Q | Options | Advised default used by this plan |\n78||---|---|---|\n79|| q1 — what to fix | real behavior / display / both / advise | **Both**: verify + fence real behavior first, then fix display (§5: backend fence precedes UI work) |\n80|| q2 — new tasks while busy | queue / reroute / manual move / advise | **Queue + reroute**: Runner refuses second assignment (`RUNNER_BUSY`); backend keeps the task claimable so another free Runner (or the same Runner when free) picks it up; no manual move needed for the common case |\n81|| q3 — what the screen shows (multi) | current task / Busy-Free / queue / memory warning | **All four**, in that priority order; memory warning is best-effort from heartbeat facts (`diskHeadroomMb`-style posture) and explicitly non-blocking |\n82|| q4 — ever allow >1 concurrent? | never / tiny background ok / if memory ok / advise | **Never** for task assignments; heartbeats/polling are the only concurrency (they are not tasks and must never render as tasks) |\n83|| q5 — what worried you in the screenshot | looked concurrent / stuck-doubled / other | Unanswered + screenshot missing → Step 0 reproduces both hypotheses (real double-hold vs stale-label display) before choosing which fix leads |\n84|\n85|If the human later answers the survey differently, only §5 Step 6 (queue /\n86|reroute policy text) and Step 7 (UI slots) need re-scoping; the per-runner\n87|fence (§5 Step 5) stands regardless.\n88|\n89|## Approach (make change easy, then make the change)\n90|\n91|Big research and structural work comes first; behavior changes land only after\n92|their seams and characterization tests exist:\n93|\n94|1. **Research first** (Steps 0–1): reproduce the two hypotheses with the\n95|   smallest possible probes; inventory every UI \"running\" signal.\n96|2. **Make change easy** (Steps 2–4): add the missing query seam\n97|   (holds-by-runner), characterization tests that pin current behavior, and a\n98|   UI audit routing every badge through `runningTask.js` — no behavior change.\n99|3. **Make the change** (Steps 5–7): backend per-runner fence, Runner-side\n100|   in-flight guard, UI single-slot clarity.\n101|4. **Assure it** (Steps 8–10): regression tests, docs, rollout/rollback.\n102|\n103|## Steps\n104|\n105|### Step 0 — Re-capture the evidence (research, first)\n106|\n107|- Re-obtain or re-create the `assets/18846.png` view: which page/widget showed\n108|  one Runner against several tasks? Touch `agent-docs/` only where a\n231|  Runner invariant is already documented; otherwise the user-facing runner\n232|  settings/monitor help text + CHANGELOG-style note per repo convention.\n233|- Record the Step 0 verdict (screenshot hypothesis) and the survey-default\n234|  decisions (§1 table) in the task folder so a later human answer can be\n235|  diffed against what shipped.\n236|\n237|### Step 10 — Rollout + rollback (assurance)\n238|\n239|- Rollout is a normal deploy (backend fence + runner update + frontend);\n240|  backend first (old Runners treat 409 `RUNNER_BUSY` as a retryable dispatch\n241|  miss — verify this fallback in Step 6 tests so mixed versions are safe).\n242|- Rollback: revert backend fence → prior caps-only behavior; no data migration\n243|  (holds stay memory-only), so rollback is stateless.\n244|- Post-deploy check: fleet with ≥2 runners, ≥2 tasks — each runner shows\n245|  BUSY with exactly one current task; queue drains without overlap.\n246|\n247|## Risks / Open Questions\n248|\n249|- Screenshot missing + survey unanswered: Step 0 re-captures evidence; §1\n250|  defaults keep the plan executable either way.\n251|- Mixed-version fleet during rollout: old Runner receiving unknown 409 code\n252|  must back off, not crash — covered in Step 6.\n253|- TTL edge: a crashed Runner's hold still blocks ITS OWN identity until TTL;\n254|  acceptable (same as today's per-task behavior), documented in Step 9.\n255|- Out of scope: raising fleet/project caps, multi-task runners by config,\n256|  real memory-based admission control (memory UI is display-only).\n257|\n258|## Validation Plan (summary)\n259|\n260|| Step | Check |\n261||---|---|\n262|| 0–1 | Verdict recorded; mixed-version backoff verified; deploy/rollback noted |\n268|\n269|Highest-risk validation: Step 1's double-dispatch probe — if it shows the\n270|backend already refuses (hypothesis (a) wrong), Steps 5–6 shrink to hardening\n271|and the plan re-weights toward the Step 4/7 display fix.\n272|\n273|## Implementation notes (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n274|\n275|Contract as shipped:\n276|\n277|- `ClaimStore.claim()` fences one live hold per Runner (race-safe backstop;\n278|  synchronous with the insert). Before anything else it\n12| *   runs the failed-boot rollback gate (Option A, ADR 0012): three crashed\n13| *   boots in a row on a staged update flip `current` back to `previous`.\n14| *   All behavior lives in test-covered units; this only wires\n15| *   env → client → daemon.\n16| * @example node runner/main.js\n17| ***/\n18|export async function main(env = process.env) {\n19|\tconst config = loadRunnerConfig(env);\n20|\tconst installRoot = installRootFor(config);\n21|\tlet boot = { action: \"boot\", state: null };\n22|\ttry {\n23|\t\tboot = bootstrapUpdateState({ installRoot });\n24|\t} catch (err) {\n25|\t\tconsole.error(`Runner update-state check failed (booting anyway): ${err?.message || err}`);\n26|\t}\n27|\tif (boot.action === \"rolled-back\") {\n28|\t\tconsole.error(\n29|\t\t\t`Runner update to ${boot.state?.to || \"unknown\"} failed to boot ${boot.state?.bootAttempts || 3}x; rolled back to the previous version.`,\n30|\t\t);\n31|\t}\n32|\tconst client = createRunnerClient({ backendUrl: config.backendUrl });\n33|\tconst summary = config.dispatch\n34|\t\t? await runDispatchLoop({ config, client })\n35|\t\t: await runSingleAssignment({ config, client });\n36|\tconsole.log(`Runner assignment done: ${JSON.stringify(summary)}`);\n37|\treturn summary;\n38|}\n39|\n40|const isEntry = process.argv[1] && import.meta.url.endsWith(process.argv[1].split(\"/\").pop() || \"\");\n41|if (isEntry) {\n42|\t// One-shot CLI: exit explicitly. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible\n6|\n7|### Principles\n8|\n9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive\n10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”\n11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)\n12|- File structure should reflect the call stack\n13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english\n14|- Include why things are done not just what is done\n15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)\n16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS\n17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality\n18|  \n19|  \n20|\n21|## Functional over Object oreintated\n22|\n23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).\n24|\n25|### Principles\n26|\n27|- Try and avoid using classes where possible\n28|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that\n29|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects\n30|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.\n31|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something\n32|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.\n33|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility\n34|\n35|\n36|## Co-location over abstraction\n37|\n38|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.\n39|\n40|### Principles\n41|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file\n42|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`\n43|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.\n44|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders\n45|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\n46|- Don’t fear repetition of code\n47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n48|- Use folders as a tool for organising\n49|\n50|## Tested over trusted \n51|\n52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n53|\n54|### Principles\n55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n58|- Tests must be consistent\n59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n61|\n62|\n63|## Fast iteration over long planning\n64|\n65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n66|\n67|### Principles\n68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n73|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.\n74|\n75|\n76|\n77|# Inspirations\n78|My principles here are inspired by:\n79|\n80|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)\n81|- Life isn’t binary (book)\n82|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)\n83|\n84|\n85|# Examples\n86|\n87|## Intent Driven descriptions\n88|\n89|### Bad Example\n90|\n91|```js\n92|\n93|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {\n94|\n95|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}\n96|\n97|    users.push(user)\n98|  \n99|}\n100|\n101|const list = []\n102|\n103|userFactory(\"Frank\",32,list)\n104|\n105|\n106|```\n107|\n108|## Good example\n109|\n110|```js\n111|\n112|/**\n113|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear\n114|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year\n115|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  \n116|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4\n117|*/\n118|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {\n119|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1\n120|  \n121|  return ageNextYear\n122|}\n123|\n124|const userObjectsList = []\n125|\n126|const usersName = \"Frank\"\n127|const usersAge = 32\n128|\n129|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})\n130|\n131|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})\n132|\n133|\n134|```","isError":false,"source":"runner-structured","runnerId":"server2-alpha","executionId":"63c8e8d5-c00b-42a1-ae1c-8f2621d54f92","seq":1},"fidelity":"normalized","seq":1,"blockId":"b1","tool":{"callId":"call_01a19dcec4267607bbabf216a39c45e1","name":"read_file","args":"{\"path\":\"docs/KB Code Standards.md\"}","result":"Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.\n1|# Values\n2|\n3|## User understandable over technical language\n4|\n5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. Even if making change easy is hard.\n74|\n75|\n76|\n77|# Inspirations\n78|My principles here are inspired by:\n79|\n80|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)\n81|- Life isn’t binary Status: plan only — no code changed.\n6|\n7|## Step 0 verdict (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n8|\n9|Screenshot `assets/18846.png` is still absent from this task folder (only\n10|`SURVEY.md` + this plan exist). Hypothesis **(a) real double-hold is PROVEN**:\n11|a throwaway probe (`/tmp/kb-step1-probe.mjs`, not committed) claimed task-A\n12|and task-B as one `runnerId` and both holds are live; the existing\n13|`api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js` flow shows the dispatch path doing the\n14|same (runner `caps-1` direct-claims task A, then dispatch assigns it task B).\n15|The suspect widget is `PerRunnerTasksWidget` (one card per assignment, no\n16|per-runner grouping), so two holds for one `runnerId` render as two live\n17|\"Runner X\" cards — the reported look. `TaskCard` likewise badges every held\n18|task `RUNNING · <runnerId>`. Hypothesis (b) stale `running_*` labels remains\n19|possible as a secondary contributor; the backend fence + grouped UI below fix\n20|(a) and display-harden (b).\n21|\n22|## Goal\n23|\n24|Guarantee that one Runner executes at most one task at a time (protecting a\n25|memory-limited dev box from concurrent-work crashes), prove the guarantee with\n26|tests, and make the single-active-task state unmistakable in the UI.\n27|\n28|## Success Criteria\n29|\n30|1. A single `runnerId` can hold at most one live backend claim at any moment;\n31|   a second claim/dispatch attempt while one is live is refused loudly\n32|   (named error code, no silent queueing inside the Runner).\n33|2. The Runner daemon cannot start a second assignment while one is in flight,\n34|   even with a stale/retried dispatch answer.\n35|3. Every UI surface derives \"running\" from one source of truth, so two tasks\n36|   can never both render as running; stale `running_*` labels render as\n37|   stale/interrupted, never as live.\n38|4. Each Runner view shows exactly one \"current task\" slot plus an explicit\n39|   Busy/Free state (and, where cheap, queued-next and memory pressure).\n40|5. `npm run test:unit` passes; new regression tests cover the per-runner fence\n41|   and the UI single-active rendering.\n42|\n43|## Context and evidence (what research found)\n44|\n45|- Embedded engine already claims single-active execution: `ExecutionQueue`\n46|  serializes jobs (`api/flow/executionQueue.js`), and\n47|  `api/flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js` characterizes \"at most one live\n48|  running_* status\".\n49|- Frontend already has the right seam: `frontend/src/components/tasks/runningTask.js`\n50|  (`resolveRunningTask`, `isTaskRunning`, `isStaleRunner`) documents the\n51|  engine-owner lock and the \"phantom-second-runner\" bug class. Open question\n52|  is whether *all* surfaces use it (audit needed).\n53|- Fleet path has the gap: `ClaimStore.claim(taskId, runnerId, …)`\n54|  (`api/flow/claimStore.js`) enforces one holder per *task*, and dispatch\n55|  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, ~L993-1060) enforces a *fleet* cap and a\n56|  *per-project* cap — but nothing enforces one live hold per *runner*.\n57|  `countLiveHolds()` supports only a `projectId` filter; there is no\n58|  by-runner lookup. Two daemon processes sharing one `runnerId`/credential\n59|  (or a claim-route call racing a dispatch lease) can therefore hand one\n60|  Runner two live assignments on a small box.\n61|- Runner daemon loop (`runner/daemon.js`, `runDispatchLoop`) is sequentially\n62|  structured (poll → execute → poll), but there is no in-process\n63|  \"assignment in flight\" guard asserted around `executeAssignment`, and no\n64|  defense against a second process with the same identity.\n65|- Per-task live-claim UI exists: `RunnerBanner.jsx` renders from `task.claim`.\n66|  If two tasks ever carry claims for the same `runnerId` (see gap above), the\n67|  UI truthfully shows the forbidden state — the screenshot's \"one Runner, many\n68|  tasks\" look. The plan below treats the survey\n72|  as open decisions with recommended defaults (§1), and Step 0 re-captures the\n73|  screenshot evidence.\n74|\n75|## How the survey shapes this plan (SURVEY.md, unanswered → advised defaults)\n76|\n77|| Survey Q | Options | Advised default used by this plan |\n78||---|---|---|\n79|| q1 — what to fix | real behavior / display / both / advise | **Both**: verify + fence real behavior first, then fix display (§5: backend fence precedes UI work) |\n80|| q2 — new tasks while busy | queue / reroute / manual move / advise | **Queue + reroute**: Runner refuses second assignment (`RUNNER_BUSY`); backend keeps the task claimable so another free Runner (or the same Runner when free) picks it up; no manual move needed for the common case |\n81|| q3 — what the screen shows (multi) | current task / Busy-Free / queue / memory warning | **All four**, in that priority order; memory warning is best-effort from heartbeat facts (`diskHeadroomMb`-style posture) and explicitly non-blocking |\n82|| q4 — ever allow >1 concurrent? The in-loop claim sites map a raced\n286|  `RUNNER_BUSY` to the same 429 instead of continuing to later candidates.\n287|- `POST /tasks/:id/claim` answers `409 RUNNER_BUSY` via the store (conflict\n288|  family, mirrors `CLAIM_CONFLICT`).\n289|- Runner daemon: explicit `RUNNER_BUSY` branch (code-first, any status)\n290|  backs off without consuming idle budget; `tryEnterAssignment` /\n291|  `leaveAssignment` single-flight guard wraps `executeAssignment` in both\n292|  the dispatch loop and the single-assignment path. }) => { freeMb: 128, low: true }\\n+ * @param {Object|null} [facts] - Runner heartbeat facts.\\n+ * @returns {{freeMb: number, low: boolean}|null}\\n+ ***/\\n+export const describeMemoryPressure = };\\n+};\\n+\\n+/***\\n+ * MARK: formatMemoryMb\\n+ * @description Human short form for a free-memory reading: megabytes below\\n+ * 1 GiB, one-decimal gigabytes above.\\n+ * @example Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.\\n- ask_user_question: Ask the user up to 4 structured questions (2-4 options each) when requirements are ambiguous\\n- workflow: Delegate substantive independent or staged work to subagents with a JavaScript workflow, optionally composing agent calls with parallel(), pipeline(), or both\\n- workflow_control: Inspect and manage workflow runs directly by canonical run ID.\\n\\nIn addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.\\n</tools>\",\"rules\":\"<rules>\\n- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find\\n- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.\\n- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.\\n- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)\\n- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls\\n- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.\\n- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.\\n- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.\\n- Use subagent_gate instead of raw subagent calls when a delegated result must be retried safely or a success quorum must be enforced.\\n- Set each subagent_gate task retrySafety to read-only only when rerunning it cannot duplicate file mutations or external side effects; omission defaults to may-write.\\n- Use workspace_session_summaries when another Pi session in the same working directory may overlap the current work.\\n- After workspace_session_summaries, compare goals, files or symbols, decisions, and next steps; when overlap is material or ownership is unclear, coordinate through intercom before writing.\\n- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.\\n- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended \\\"Type something.\\\" row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author \\\"Other\\\" or \\\"Type something.\\\" labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.\\n- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The \\\"Type something.\\\" row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append \\\"(Recommended)\\\" to its label.\\n- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.\\n- The `workflow` tool runs multi-agent orchestration — it fans decomposable work out across subagents, and fits tasks shaped like: repo-wide inspection, independent parallel research/checks, multi-perspective review, or fan-out/fan-in synthesis. ONLY call it when the user explicitly opts in — via the workflow trigger word, `/workflows run`, or their own words (e.g. 'run a workflow', 'fan this out', '并行审一遍'). Do not pad with large unchanged regions.\\\\n- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.\\\\n- Use subagent_gate instead of raw subagent calls when a delegated result must be retried safely or a success quorum must be enforced.\\\\n- Set each subagent_gate task retrySafety to read-only only when rerunning it cannot duplicate file mutations or external side effects; omission defaults to may-write.\\\\n- Use workspace_session_summaries when another Pi session in the same working directory may overlap the current work.\\\\n- After workspace_session_summaries, compare goals, files or symbols, decisions, and next steps; when overlap is material or ownership is unclear, coordinate through intercom before writing.\\\\n- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.\\\\n- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended \\\\\\\"Type something.\\\\\\\" row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author \\\\\\\"Other\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"Type something.\\\\\\\" labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.\\\\n- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The \\\\\\\"Type something.\\\\\\\" row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append \\\\\\\"(Recommended)\\\\\\\" to its label.\\\\n- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.\\\\n- The `workflow` tool runs multi-agent orchestration — it fans decomposable work out across subagents, and fits tasks shaped like: repo-wide inspection, independent parallel research/checks, multi-perspective review, or fan-out/fan-in synthesis. ONLY call it when the user explicitly opts in — via the workflow trigger word, `/workflows run`, or their own words (e.g. 'run a workflow', 'fan this out', '并行审一遍'). Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.\\\\n- ask_user_question: Ask the user up to 4 structured questions (2-4 options each) when requirements are ambiguous\\\\n- workflow: Delegate substantive independent or staged work to subagents with a JavaScript workflow, optionally composing agent calls with parallel(), pipeline(), or both\\\\n- workflow_control: Inspect and manage workflow runs directly by canonical run ID.\\\\n\\\\nIn addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.\\\\n</tools>\\\",\\\"rules\\\":\\\"<rules>\\\\n- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find\\\\n- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.\\\\n- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.\\\\n- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)\\\\n- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls\\\\n- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.\\\\n- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.\\\\n- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.\\\\n- Use subagent_gate instead of raw subagent calls when a delegated result must be retried safely or a success quorum must be enforced.\\\\n- Set each subagent_gate task retrySafety to read-only only when rerunning it cannot duplicate file mutations or external side effects; omission defaults to may-write.\\\\n- Use workspace_session_summaries when another Pi session in the same working directory may overlap the current work.\\\\n- After workspace_session_summaries, compare goals, files or symbols, decisions, and next steps; when overlap is material or ownership is unclear, coordinate through intercom before writing.\\\\n- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.\\\\n- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended \\\\\\\"Type something.\\\\\\\" row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author \\\\\\\"Other\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"Type something.\\\\\\\" labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.\\\\n- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The \\\\\\\"Type something.\\\\\\\" row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append \\\\\\\"(Recommended)\\\\\\\" to its label.\\\\n- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.\\\\n- The `workflow` tool runs multi-agent orchestration — it fans decomposable work out across subagents, and fits tasks shaped like: repo-wide inspection, independent parallel research/checks, multi-perspective review, or fan-out/fan-in synthesis. ONLY call it when the user explicitly opts in — via the workflow trigger word, `/workflows run`, or their own words (e.g. 'run a workflow', 'fan this out', '并行审一遍'). For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit — do not call it; you may briefly offer it (with a rough cost) as an option instead.\\\\n- Use workflow_control for workflow lifecycle management; do not ask the user to type /workflows when this tool can perform the action.\\\\n- Use stop to terminate or quit a run. Closing the navigator does not stop a run.\\\\n- Be concise in your responses\\\\n- Show file paths clearly when working with files\\\\n</rules>\\\",\\\"docs\\\":\\\"<docs>\\\\nPi documentation (read Implementation Plan — One task per Runner at a time (+ unambiguous UI)\n\nTask: `0faa3d87-fd70-402d-839f-e2cced302d9b`\n(\"UI seems to imply a runner is running multiple tasks at once\")\nAuthor: planning stage, 2026-11-02. Status: plan only — no code changed.\n\n## Step 0 verdict (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n\nScreenshot `assets/18846.png` is still absent from this task folder (only\n`SURVEY.md` + this plan exist). Hypothesis **(a) real double-hold is PROVEN**:\na throwaway probe (`/tmp/kb-step1-probe.mjs`, not committed) claimed task-A\nand task-B as one `runnerId` and both holds are live; the existing\n`api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js` flow shows the dispatch path doing the\nsame (runner `caps-1` direct-claims task A, then dispatch assigns it task B).\nThe suspect widget is `PerRunnerTasksWidget` (one card per assignment, no\nper-runner grouping), so two holds for one `runnerId` render as two live\n\"Runner X\" cards — the reported look. `TaskCard` likewise badges every held\ntask `RUNNING · <runnerId>`. Hypothesis (b) stale `running_*` labels remains\npossible as a secondary contributor; the backend fence + grouped UI below fix\n(a) and display-harden (b).\n\n## Goal\n\nGuarantee that one Runner executes at most one task at a time (protecting a\nmemory-limited dev box from concurrent-work crashes), prove the guarantee with\ntests, and make the single-active-task state unmistakable in the UI.\n\n## Success Criteria\n\n1. A single `runnerId` can hold at most one live backend claim at any moment;\n   a second claim/dispatch attempt while one is live is refused loudly\n   (named error code, no silent queueing inside the Runner).\n2. The Runner daemon cannot start a second assignment while one is in flight,\n   even with a stale/retried dispatch answer.\n3. Every UI surface derives \"running\" from one source of truth, so two tasks\n   can never both render as running; stale `running_*` labels render as\n   stale/interrupted, never as live.\n4. Each Runner view shows exactly one \"current task\" slot plus an explicit\n   Busy/Free state (and, where cheap, queued-next and memory pressure).\n5. `npm run test:unit` passes; new regression tests cover the per-runner fence\n   and the UI single-active rendering.\n\n## Context and evidence (what research found)\n\n- Embedded engine already claims single-active execution: `ExecutionQueue`\n  serializes jobs (`api/flow/executionQueue.js`), and\n  `api/flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js` characterizes \"at most one live\n  running_* status\".\n- Frontend already has the right seam: `frontend/src/components/tasks/runningTask.js`\n  (`resolveRunningTask`, `isTaskRunning`, `isStaleRunner`) documents the\n  engine-owner lock and the \"phantom-second-runner\" bug class. Open question\n  is whether *all* surfaces use it (audit needed).\n- Fleet path has the gap: `ClaimStore.claim(taskId, runnerId, …)`\n  (`api/flow/claimStore.js`) enforces one holder per *task*, and dispatch\n  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, ~L993-1060) enforces a *fleet* cap and a\n  *per-project* cap — but nothing enforces one live hold per *runner*.\n  `countLiveHolds()` supports only a `projectId` filter; there is no\n  by-runner lookup. Status: plan only — no code changed.\n\n## Step 0 verdict (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n\nScreenshot `assets/18846.png` is still absent from this task folder (only\n`SURVEY.md` + this plan exist). Hypothesis **(a) real double-hold is PROVEN**:\na throwaway probe (`/tmp/kb-step1-probe.mjs`, not committed) claimed task-A\nand task-B as one `runnerId` and both holds are live; the existing\n`api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js` flow shows the dispatch path doing the\nsame (runner `caps-1` direct-claims task A, then dispatch assigns it task B).\nThe suspect widget is `PerRunnerTasksWidget` (one card per assignment, no\nper-runner grouping), so two holds for one `runnerId` render as two live\n\"Runner X\" cards — the reported look. `TaskCard` likewise badges every held\ntask `RUNNING · <runnerId>`. Hypothesis (b) stale `running_*` labels remains\npossible as a secondary contributor; the backend fence + grouped UI below fix\n(a) and display-harden (b).\n\n## Goal\n\nGuarantee that one Runner executes at most one task at a time (protecting a\nmemory-limited dev box from concurrent-work crashes), prove the guarantee with\ntests, and make the single-active-task state unmistakable in the UI.\n\n## Success Criteria\n\n1. A single `runnerId` can hold at most one live backend claim at any moment;\n   a second claim/dispatch attempt while one is live is refused loudly\n   (named error code, no silent queueing inside the Runner).\n2. The Runner daemon cannot start a second assignment while one is in flight,\n   even with a stale/retried dispatch answer.\n3. Every UI surface derives \"running\" from one source of truth, so two tasks\n   can never both render as running; stale `running_*` labels render as\n   stale/interrupted, never as live.\n4. Each Runner view shows exactly one \"current task\" slot plus an explicit\n   Busy/Free state (and, where cheap, queued-next and memory pressure).\n5. `npm run test:unit` passes; new regression tests cover the per-runner fence\n   and the UI single-active rendering.\n\n## Context and evidence (what research found)\n\n- Embedded engine already claims single-active execution: `ExecutionQueue`\n  serializes jobs (`api/flow/executionQueue.js`), and\n  `api/flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js` characterizes \"at most one live\n  running_* status\".\n- Frontend already has the right seam: `frontend/src/components/tasks/runningTask.js`\n  (`resolveRunningTask`, `isTaskRunning`, `isStaleRunner`) documents the\n  engine-owner lock and the \"phantom-second-runner\" bug class. Open question\n  is whether *all* surfaces use it (audit needed).\n- Fleet path has the gap: `ClaimStore.claim(taskId, runnerId, …)`\n  (`api/flow/claimStore.js`) enforces one holder per *task*, and dispatch\n  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, ~L993-1060) enforces a *fleet* cap and a\n  *per-project* cap — but nothing enforces one live hold per *runner*.\n  `countLiveHolds()` supports only a `projectId` filter; there is no\n  by-runner lookup. Two daemon processes sharing one `runnerId`/credential\n  (or a claim-route call racing a dispatch lease) can therefore hand one\n  Runner two live assignments on a small box.\n- Runner daemon loop (`runner/daemon.js`, `runDispatchLoop`) is sequentially\n  structured (poll → execute → poll), but there is no in-process\n  \"assignment in flight\" guard asserted around `executeAssignment`, and no\n  defense against a second process with the same identity.\n- Per-task live-claim UI exists: `RunnerBanner.jsx` renders from `task.claim`.\n  If two tasks ever carry claims for the same `runnerId` (see gap above), the\n  UI truthfully shows the forbidden state — the screenshot's \"one Runner, many\n  tasks\" look. Stale `running_*` labels are the second suspect (display-only).\n- Evidence gaps: the screenshot (`assets/18846.png`) is NOT present in this\n  task's docs folder (only `SURVEY.md` exists), and `SURVEY.md` has\n  `\"answers\": {}` (all questions unanswered). Fleet surfaces:\n`PerRunnerTasksWidget` was the ungrouped surface (fixed);\n`RunnerConfigurationSection` and `NowPlayingBar` already deduped per\nRunner (kept, plus explicit Busy/Free); `TaskCard` `RUNNING · runner` and\n`RunnerBanner` stay per-task truthful, with banner copy now stating the\nRunner is busy with that task alone.\n\nTests added/updated: `claimStore.test.js` (+4), new\n`runnerBusy.test.js` (4), `runnerDispatchCaps.test.js` (reworked to\ndistinct Runners + busy/fleet precedence), `runnerRoutes.test.js`\n(second-dispatch 429), `daemon.test.js` (+5: busy backoff, stale-retry\nrefusal backoff, guard ×2, memory), new `runnerSlots.test.js` (7),\nwidget (+3), settings (+4),\n`NowPlayingBar.test.jsx` (+4 assertions), `RunnerBanner.test.jsx`\n(copy pins).\n","durationMs":1}},{"id":8,"ts":"2026-11-03T07:49:02.480Z","feed":"tools","feeds":["tools"],"kind":"tool","turn":2,"text":"[RESULT] # Implementation Plan — One task per Runner at a time (+ unambiguous UI) Task: `0faa3d87-fd70-402d-839f-e2cced302d9b` (\"UI seems to imply a runner is running multiple tasks at once\") Author: planning stage, 2026-11-02. Hypothesis **(a) real double-hold is PROVEN**: a throwaway probe (`/tmp/kb-step1-probe.mjs`, not committed) claimed task-A and task-B as one `runnerId` and both holds are… (1ms)","meta":{"toolName":"read","toolCallId":"call_dtpgiol9","durationMs":1,"source":"runner-structured","runnerId":"local-alpha","executionId":"242a5afd-0a37-4bfd-8850-3efd68bec80f","seq":2},"fidelity":"normalized","seq":8,"tool":{"callId":"call_dtpgiol9","name":"read","result":"# Implementation Plan — One task per Runner at a time (+ unambiguous UI)\n\nTask: `0faa3d87-fd70-402d-839f-e2cced302d9b`\n(\"UI seems to imply a runner is running multiple tasks at once\")\nAuthor: planning stage, 2026-11-02. Status: plan only — no code changed.\n\n## Step 0 verdict (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n\nScreenshot `assets/18846.png` is still absent from this task folder (only\n`SURVEY.md` + this plan exist). Hypothesis **(a) real double-hold is PROVEN**:\na throwaway probe (`/tmp/kb-step1-probe.mjs`, not committed) claimed task-A\nand task-B as one `runnerId` and both holds are live; the existing\n`api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js` flow shows the dispatch path doing the\nsame (runner `caps-1` direct-claims task A, then dispatch assigns it task B).\nThe suspect widget is `PerRunnerTasksWidget` (one card per assignment, no\nper-runner grouping), so two holds for one `runnerId` render as two live\n\"Runner X\" cards — the reported look. `TaskCard` likewise badges every held\ntask `RUNNING · <runnerId>`. Hypothesis (b) stale `running_*` labels remains\npossible as a secondary contributor; the backend fence + grouped UI below fix\n(a) and display-harden (b).\n\n## Goal\n\nGuarantee that one Runner executes at most one task at a time (protecting a\nmemory-limited dev box from concurrent-work crashes), prove the guarantee with\ntests, and make the single-active-task state unmistakable in the UI.\n\n## Success Criteria\n\n1. A single `runnerId` can hold at most one live backend claim at any moment;\n   a second claim/dispatch attempt while one is live is refused loudly\n   (named error code, no silent queueing inside the Runner).\n2. The Runner daemon cannot start a second assignment while one is in flight,\n   even with a stale/retried dispatch answer.\n3. Every UI surface derives \"running\" from one source of truth, so two tasks\n   can never both render as running; stale `running_*` labels render as\n   stale/interrupted, never as live.\n4. Each Runner view shows exactly one \"current task\" slot plus an explicit\n   Busy/Free state (and, where cheap, queued-next and memory pressure).\n5. `npm run test:unit` passes; new regression tests cover the per-runner fence\n   and the UI single-active rendering.\n\n## Context and evidence (what research found)\n\n- Embedded engine already claims single-active execution: `ExecutionQueue`\n  serializes jobs (`api/flow/executionQueue.js`), and\n  `api/flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js` characterizes \"at most one live\n  running_* status\".\n- Frontend already has the right seam: `frontend/src/components/tasks/runningTask.js`\n  (`resolveRunningTask`, `isTaskRunning`, `isStaleRunner`) documents the\n  engine-owner lock and the \"phantom-second-runner\" bug class. Open question\n  is whether *all* surfaces use it (audit needed).\n- Fleet path has the gap: `ClaimStore.claim(taskId, runnerId, …)`\n  (`api/flow/claimStore.js`) enforces one holder per *task*, and dispatch\n  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, ~L993-1060) enforces a *fleet* cap and a\n  *per-project* cap — but nothing enforces one live hold per *runner*.\n  `countLiveHolds()` supports only a `projectId` filter; there is no\n  by-runner lookup. Two daemon processes sharing one `runnerId`/credential\n  (or a claim-route call racing a dispatch lease) can therefore hand one\n  Runner two live assignments on a small box.\n- Runner daemon loop (`runner/daemon.js`, `runDispatchLoop`) is sequentially\n  structured (poll → execute → poll), but there is no in-process\n  \"assignment in flight\" guard asserted around `executeAssignment`, and no\n  defense against a second process with the same identity.\n- Per-task live-claim UI exists: `RunnerBanner.jsx` renders from `task.claim`.\n  If two tasks ever carry claims for the same `runnerId` (see gap above), the\n  UI truthfully shows the forbidden state — the screenshot's \"one Runner, many\n  tasks\" look. Stale `running_*` labels are the second suspect (display-only).\n- Evidence gaps: the screenshot (`assets/18846.png`) is NOT present in this\n  task's docs folder (only `SURVEY.md` exists), and `SURVEY.md` has\n  `\"answers\": {}` (all questions unanswered). The plan below treats the survey\n  as open decisions with recommended defaults (§1), and Step 0 re-captures the\n  screenshot evidence.\n\n## How the survey shapes this plan (SURVEY.md, unanswered → advised defaults)\n\n| Survey Q | Options | Advised default used by this plan |\n|---|---|---|\n| q1 — what to fix | real behavior / display / both / advise | **Both**: verify + fence real behavior first, then fix display (§5: backend fence precedes UI work) |\n| q2 — new tasks while busy | queue / reroute / manual move / advise | **Queue + reroute**: Runner refuses second assignment (`RUNNER_BUSY`); backend keeps the task claimable so another free Runner (or the same Runner when free) picks it up; no manual move needed for the common case |\n| q3 — what the screen shows (multi) | current task / Busy-Free / queue / memory warning | **All four**, in that priority order; memory warning is best-effort from heartbeat facts (`diskHeadroomMb`-style posture) and explicitly non-blocking |\n| q4 — ever allow >1 concurrent? | never / tiny background ok / if memory ok / advise | **Never** for task assignments; heartbeats/polling are the only concurrency (they are not tasks and must never render as tasks) |\n| q5 — what worried you in the screenshot | looked concurrent / stuck-doubled / other | Unanswered + screenshot missing → Step 0 reproduces both hypotheses (real double-hold vs stale-label display) before choosing which fix leads |\n\nIf the human later answers the survey differently, only §5 Step 6 (queue /\nreroute policy text) and Step 7 (UI slots) need re-scoping; the per-runner\nfence (§5 Step 5) stands regardless.\n\n## Approach (make change easy, then make the change)\n\nBig research and structural work comes first; behavior changes land only after\ntheir seams and characterization tests exist:\n\n1. **Research first** (Steps 0–1): reproduce the two hypotheses with the\n   smallest possible probes; inventory every UI \"running\" signal.\n2. **Make change easy** (Steps 2–4): add the missing query seam\n   (holds-by-runner), characterization tests that pin current behavior, and a\n   UI audit routing every badge through `runningTask.js` — no behavior change.\n3. **Make the change** (Steps 5–7): backend per-runner fence, Runner-side\n   in-flight guard, UI single-slot clarity.\n4. **Assure it** (Steps 8–10): regression tests, docs, rollout/rollback.\n\n## Steps\n\n### Step 0 — Re-capture the evidence (research, first)\n\n- Re-obtain or re-create the `assets/18846.png` view: which page/widget showed\n  one Runner against several tasks? If the reporter can re-attach it, file it\n  under this task's `assets/`; otherwise reproduce via\n  `npm run capture:screenshot` against a fixture with two claim-carrying tasks\n  for the same `runnerId` (see Step 1 probe).\n- Decide which hypothesis the screenshot shows: (a) two live claims, one\n  `runnerId` (backend gap), or (b) one live claim + stale `running_*` labels\n  (display gap). Record the verdict at the top of this file before Step 5.\n- Validation: the recorded verdict names the page, the tasks, and which\n  hypothesis; a reviewer can re-open the same view.\n\n### Step 1 — Minimal reproduction probes (research, first)\n\n- Backend probe (throwaway, `/tmp`, not committed): drive `ClaimStore`\n  directly — claim task A as `runner-1`, then claim task B as `runner-1` —\n  and show both holds are live today. Then drive `POST /runners/dispatch`\n  twice for one `runnerId` with two claimable tasks and show whether two\n  leases are issued (mirror the style of\n  `api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`).\n- Frontend probe: render the suspect view with one engine-owner task plus a\n  second task carrying a stale `running_agent` label; note every element that\n  renders a live-looking RUNNING/claimed signal.\n- Validation: probes are independent of the later fix (they use public\n  routes/helpers); keep the backend probe's assertions to convert into the\n  Step 8 regression test.\n\n### Step 2 — Add the by-runner query seam (make change easy, no behavior change)\n\n- `api/flow/claimStore.js`: add `liveHoldsByRunner(runnerId)` (and optionally\n  extend `countLiveHolds({ runnerId })`), reusing the existing lazy-expiry\n  sweep in `_holding()`. Pure query — no call-site behavior changes.\n- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`: expose the data the UI needs — extend the\n  existing `liveAssignments` projection (~L468) or the runner-status payload\n  with `currentTaskId` / `liveHoldCount` per runner so the UI never joins\n  claims client-side.\n- Validation: `npm run test:api -- claimStore` passes; new unit tests assert\n  expiry-aware by-runner counts.\n\n### Step 3 — Characterization tests pinning current behavior (make change easy)\n\n- Add failing-or-pinning tests *before* the fence: \"second dispatch for a\n  busy runnerId is refused\" (expectation set to the DESIRED code, allowed to\n  fail until Step 5 — mark clearly as fence-pending), plus passing\n  characterization of today's fleet/project caps to prevent regressions.\n- Frontend: add a test rendering two claim/stale-running tasks for one runner\n  through the real view (not the helper in isolation) pinning today's\n  (wrong-looking) output, to flip in Step 7.\n- Validation: full `npm run test:unit` green except the explicitly-marked\n  fence-pending assertions.\n\n### Step 4 — UI signal audit + route every badge through the one helper (make change easy)\n\n- Inventory every \"running/live/claimed\" signal: `TaskCard`, `RunnerBanner`,\n  `ObservabilityDashboard`, `EngineStatePill`, `MobileMonitorView`,\n  `TaskDetailOverlay`, activity console — record which use\n  `resolveRunningTask`/`isTaskRunning`/`isStaleRunner` and which read raw\n  `task.status`/`task.claim`.\n- Convert stragglers to the helpers with NO visual redesign yet: stale labels\n  must already render as stale/interrupted after this step.\n- Validation: `npm run test:frontend` passes; the Step 1 frontend probe now\n  shows at most one live RUNNING badge.\n\n### Step 5 — Backend: one live hold per runner (make the change)\n\n- In `claim()`-issuing paths (`POST /runners/dispatch` candidate loop AND the\n  direct single-assignment claim route ~L846, AND the merge-lease path\n  ~L1067): refuse when the requesting `runnerId` already holds a live,\n  unexpired hold. Suggested contract: HTTP 409 + code `RUNNER_BUSY` with the\n  current `taskId`/`executionId` in the body (mirrors existing `CLAIM_CONFLICT`\n  / `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED` shapes).\n- Keep the refused task claimable (do NOT park it on the busy runner) so q2's\n  queue+reroute default holds: another free Runner can claim it; the busy\n  Runner's next poll after completing gets fresh work.\n- Decide + document TTL interplay: an expired hold must not block (lazy sweep\n  already handles this); a crashed Runner's hold blocks re-dispatch only until\n  TTL, same as today — no new resurrection logic.\n- Validation: fence-pending tests from Step 3 now pass; caps tests\n  (`runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`) and `singleActiveInvariant.test.js` still pass.\n\n### Step 6 — Runner daemon: in-flight guard + busy handling (make the change)\n\n- `runner/daemon.js`: assert a single-flight guard around `executeAssignment`\n  in `runDispatchLoop` (and the single-assignment path): never start a second\n  assignment while `state.executionId` is set; treat a second dispatch answer\n  arriving mid-run as a bug and back off rather than executing.\n- Handle `RUNNER_BUSY` like `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED`: log, back off\n  without consuming idle budget, re-poll (covers the two-processes-one-identity\n  case: the loser backs off instead of double-executing).\n- Optional hardening (only if Step 1 shows it is reachable): local pid/lockfile\n  so two daemons with the same `runnerId` on one box cannot both run; document\n  as defense-in-depth, not the primary fence (the backend fence is primary).\n- Validation: `runner/daemon.test.js` additions — busy answer backs off;\n  in-flight guard never double-executes (mirror the existing 429 test ~L1024).\n\n### Step 7 — UI: one unmistakable current-task slot per Runner (make the change)\n\n- Per Runner (settings/runners list + monitor): exactly one \"Current task\"\n  slot (task link + stage + elapsed), an explicit `BUSY`/`FREE` pill sourced\n  from the Step 2 payload (`liveHoldCount`/`currentTaskId`), a \"queued next\"\n  count when work is waiting, and a best-effort memory-pressure note from\n  heartbeat posture. Never render two live task rows under one Runner.\n- Keep `RunnerBanner` per task (it answers \"where is THIS task running\") but\n  ensure its copy cannot imply the Runner is otherwise free; link to the\n  Runner's single slot.\n- Validation: headless check via existing fixtures + `npm run capture:screenshot`\n  (no long-lived servers); flip the Step 3 frontend test to the new rendering.\n\n### Step 8 — Regression tests (assurance)\n\n- Backend: busy-runner dispatch refused (agent + merge + direct-claim paths);\n  refused task still claimable by a different runner; expired hold does not\n  block; two processes / double-poll with one identity cannot double-execute.\n- Frontend: one-runner-two-tasks fixture renders exactly one BUSY slot and one\n  live badge; stale labels render stale.\n- Runner: `RUNNER_BUSY` backoff; single-flight guard.\n- Gate: `npm run test:unit` fully green; run the touched suites\n  (`claimStore`, `runnerRoutes`, `runnerDispatchCaps`, `singleActiveInvariant`,\n  `daemon`, `runningTask`, dashboard) unmodified, no narrowing/deselect.\n\n### Step 9 — Documentation (assurance)\n\n- Update the Runner/operator docs: the one-task-per-Runner invariant, the\n  `RUNNER_BUSY` contract (code, status, retry-after behavior), queue+reroute\n  semantics, and what each UI slot means. Touch `agent-docs/` only where a\n  Runner invariant is already documented; otherwise the user-facing runner\n  settings/monitor help text + CHANGELOG-style note per repo convention.\n- Record the Step 0 verdict (screenshot hypothesis) and the survey-default\n  decisions (§1 table) in the task folder so a later human answer can be\n  diffed against what shipped.\n\n### Step 10 — Rollout + rollback (assurance)\n\n- Rollout is a normal deploy (backend fence + runner update + frontend);\n  backend first (old Runners treat 409 `RUNNER_BUSY` as a retryable dispatch\n  miss — verify this fallback in Step 6 tests so mixed versions are safe).\n- Rollback: revert backend fence → prior caps-only behavior; no data migration\n  (holds stay memory-only), so rollback is stateless.\n- Post-deploy check: fleet with ≥2 runners, ≥2 tasks — each runner shows\n  BUSY with exactly one current task; queue drains without overlap.\n\n## Risks / Open Questions\n\n- Screenshot missing + survey unanswered: Step 0 re-captures evidence; §1\n  defaults keep the plan executable either way.\n- Mixed-version fleet during rollout: old Runner receiving unknown 409 code\n  must back off, not crash — covered in Step 6.\n- TTL edge: a crashed Runner's hold still blocks ITS OWN identity until TTL;\n  acceptable (same as today's per-task behavior), documented in Step 9.\n- Out of scope: raising fleet/project caps, multi-task runners by config,\n  real memory-based admission control (memory UI is display-only).\n\n## Validation Plan (summary)\n\n| Step | Check |\n|---|---|\n| 0–1 | Verdict recorded; throwaway probes reproduce the bug via public routes |\n| 2–4 | `npm run test:api`, `npm run test:frontend` green; ≤1 live badge in probe |\n| 5–6 | Fence tests pass; caps + invariant + daemon suites unmodified-green |\n| 7 | Headless screenshot of runner view shows one BUSY slot |\n| 8 | Full `npm run test:unit` green |\n| 9–10 | Docs updated; mixed-version backoff verified; deploy/rollback noted |\n\nHighest-risk validation: Step 1's double-dispatch probe — if it shows the\nbackend already refuses (hypothesis (a) wrong), Steps 5–6 shrink to hardening\nand the plan re-weights toward the Step 4/7 display fix.\n\n## Implementation notes (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n\nContract as shipped:\n\n- `ClaimStore.claim()` fences one live hold per Runner (race-safe backstop;\n  synchronous with the insert). Same-task re-claim stays `CLAIM_CONFLICT`;\n  a second task answers `409 RUNNER_BUSY` with\n  `holder: { runnerId, taskId, executionId, epoch }`.\n- `POST /runners/dispatch` refuses a busy Runner with **`429 RUNNER_BUSY`**\n  (deviation from the plan's suggested 409: the daemon crashes on unknown\n  409 codes but backs off on any 429, so 429 is what keeps mixed-version\n  fleets safe per Step 10; it also matches the fleet-cap backpressure\n  family the daemon already handles). The in-loop claim sites map a raced\n  `RUNNER_BUSY` to the same 429 instead of continuing to later candidates.\n- `POST /tasks/:id/claim` answers `409 RUNNER_BUSY` via the store (conflict\n  family, mirrors `CLAIM_CONFLICT`).\n- Runner daemon: explicit `RUNNER_BUSY` branch (code-first, any status)\n  backs off without consuming idle budget; `tryEnterAssignment` /\n  `leaveAssignment` single-flight guard wraps `executeAssignment` in both\n  the dispatch loop and the single-assignment path. The `STALE_RUNNER`\n  heartbeat-then-retry path also backs off (no idle-budget burn, no crash)\n  when the retry itself is refused with `RUNNER_BUSY` / 429 / `RUNNER_PAUSED`\n  — e.g. a duplicate daemon sharing the identity — instead of letting the\n  refusal escape and kill the loop. No pid/lockfile: the\n  backend fence is primary and sufficient, and stale locks would be a new\n  failure mode on a crash-prone dev box.\n- `GET /runners/monitor` gains `runnerLoad` (one row per busy Runner:\n  `runnerId`, `liveHoldCount`, `currentTaskId`, `currentExecutionId`,\n  `currentStageId`, `startedAt`). UI groups through the shared\n  `groupLiveAssignments` helper (`frontend/.../widgets/runnerSlots.js`),\n  falling back to grouping `liveAssignments` when `runnerLoad` is absent.\n- Heartbeat facts gain display-only `memoryFreeMb` (no backend change\n  needed: facts flow wholesale; `normalizeCapabilities` ignores it).\n- Queued-next: no per-Runner queue exists (any free Runner takes waiting\n  work); the fleet-level \"N deferred to Runners\" scheduler line already\n  covers the waiting-work signal, so no new queue count was added.\n- Merge-kind dispatch has no HTTP-level test fixture (needs real git\n  remotes); it shares the fenced dispatch entry + store claim, both\n  covered. Direct `/runners/integration/acquire` is lease-only (no task\n  claim) and out of fence scope.\n\nUI audit (Step 4): embedded-engine surfaces (`TaskCard`, dashboard,\n`TaskDetail*`, `StageColumn`, `EngineStatePill`, `MobileMonitorView`,\n`NowPlayingBar` legacy display) already derive running state from\n`runningTask.js` / engine-owner helpers — no change. The plan below treats the survey\\n  as open decisions with recommended defaults (§1), and Step 0 re-captures the\\n  screenshot evidence.\\n\\n## How the survey shapes this plan (SURVEY.md, unanswered → advised defaults)\\n\\n| Survey Q | Options | Advised default used by this plan |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| q1 — what to fix | real behavior / display / both / advise | **Both**: verify + fence real behavior first, then fix display (§5: backend fence precedes UI work) |\\n| q2 — new tasks while busy | queue / reroute / manual move / advise | **Queue + reroute**: Runner refuses second assignment (`RUNNER_BUSY`); backend keeps the task claimable so another free Runner (or the same Runner when free) picks it up; no manual move needed for the common case |\\n| q3 — what the screen shows (multi) | current task / Busy-Free / queue / memory warning | **All four**, in that priority order; memory warning is best-effort from heartbeat facts (`diskHeadroomMb`-style posture) and explicitly non-blocking |\\n| q4 — ever allow >1 concurrent? | never / tiny background ok / if memory ok / advise | **Never** for task assignments; heartbeats/polling are the only concurrency (they are not tasks and must never render as tasks) |\\n| q5 — what worried you in the screenshot | looked concurrent / stuck-doubled / other | Unanswered + screenshot missing → Step 0 reproduces both hypotheses (real double-hold vs stale-label display) before choosing which fix leads |\\n\\nIf the human later answers the survey differently, only §5 Step 6 (queue /\\nreroute policy text) and Step 7 (UI slots) need re-scoping; the per-runner\\nfence (§5 Step 5) stands regardless.\\n\\n## Approach (make change easy, then make the change)\\n\\nBig research and structural work comes first; behavior changes land only after\\ntheir seams and characterization tests exist:\\n\\n1. **Research first** (Steps 0–1): reproduce the two hypotheses with the\\n   smallest possible probes; inventory every UI \\\"running\\\" signal.\\n2. **Make change easy** (Steps 2–4): add the missing query seam\\n   (holds-by-runner), characterization tests that pin current behavior, and a\\n   UI audit routing every badge through `runningTask.js` — no behavior change.\\n3. **Make the change** (Steps 5–7): backend per-runner fence, Runner-side\\n   in-flight guard, UI single-slot clarity.\\n4. **Assure it** (Steps 8–10): regression tests, docs, rollout/rollback.\\n\\n## Steps\\n\\n### Step 0 — Re-capture the evidence (research, first)\\n\\n- Re-obtain or re-create the `assets/18846.png` view: which page/widget showed\\n  one Runner against several tasks? Event `prompted` may carry the exact stage `prompt` (capped at 20k chars) plus the serving `harness`/`model` for the monitor's with-prompt cards. |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/logs` | Runner-only: ingest one sequenced log frame (gaps marked, never hidden). |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/log-events` | Runner-only: ingest one sequenced batch of normalized agent events (1–200 per batch; tool calls/results with args, thinking, usage, permissions, plans, errors with per-step timings) processed into the same canonical records as the embedded path. |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/complete-execution` | Runner-only: idempotent completion with epoch fence and SHA check; releases the lease and applies the engine-owned finish (report, survey park, failure routing, advance). |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/claim-heartbeat` | Runner-only: renew a live claim mid-stage (extends the lease TTL; 409 `STALE_EPOCH` when superseded) so long harness runs keep their fence. |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/interrupt` | Runner-only: park a task as interrupted and drop its lease. Optional `reason` is recorded in task history (e.g. workdir-cap refusals). |\n| POST | `/runners/integration/acquire` | Runner-only: lease the head queued integration for a project + target branch (200 `leased` + `executionId`/`epoch`, 200 unassigned when empty, 409 `INTEGRATION_BUSY` when a live lease is held). Refuses Runners the head task's stage does not allow (409 `RUNNER_NOT_ALLOWED` / `RUNNER_BLOCKED`, without leasing). |\n| POST | `/runners/integration/heartbeat` | Runner-only: renew a live integration lease (409 `STALE_EPOCH` when superseded). |\n| POST | `/runners/integration/report` | Runner-only: terminal integration report (`landed`/`conflict`/`stale-head`/`needs-sync`/`failed`; idempotent re-reports, stale executions rejected). |\n| GET | `/runners/integration` | Per-scope integration queue depth, live lease, and global lease counters. |\n\n[221 more lines in file. Event `prompted` may carry the exact stage `prompt` (capped at 20k chars) plus the serving `harness`/`model` for the monitor's with-prompt cards. |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/logs` | Runner-only: ingest one sequenced log frame (gaps marked, never hidden). |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/log-events` | Runner-only: ingest one sequenced batch of normalized agent events (1–200 per batch; tool calls/results with args, thinking, usage, permissions, plans, errors with per-step timings) processed into the same canonical records as the embedded path. |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/complete-execution` | Runner-only: idempotent completion with epoch fence and SHA check; releases the lease and applies the engine-owned finish (report, survey park, failure routing, advance). |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/claim-heartbeat` | Runner-only: renew a live claim mid-stage (extends the lease TTL; 409 `STALE_EPOCH` when superseded) so long harness runs keep their fence. |\n| POST | `/tasks/:id/interrupt` | Runner-only: park a task as interrupted and drop its lease. Optional `reason` is recorded in task history (e.g. workdir-cap refusals). |\n| POST | `/runners/integration/acquire` | Runner-only: lease the head queued integration for a project + target branch (200 `leased` + `executionId`/`epoch`, 200 unassigned when empty, 409 `INTEGRATION_BUSY` when a live lease is held). Refuses Runners the head task's stage does not allow (409 `RUNNER_NOT_ALLOWED` / `RUNNER_BLOCKED`, without leasing). |\n| POST | `/runners/integration/heartbeat` | Runner-only: renew a live integration lease (409 `STALE_EPOCH` when superseded). |\n| POST | `/runners/integration/report` | Runner-only: terminal integration report (`landed`/`conflict`/`stale-head`/`needs-sync`/`failed`; idempotent re-reports, stale executions rejected). |\n| GET | `/runners/integration` | Per-scope integration queue depth, live lease, and global lease counters. |\n\n[221 more lines in file.
