`0faa3d87-fd70-402d-839f-e2cced302d9b`\n4|(\"UI seems to imply a runner is running multiple tasks at once\")\n5|Author: planning stage, 2026-11-02. Status: plan only — no code changed.\n6|\n7|## Step 0 verdict (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n8|\n9|Screenshot `assets/18846.png` is still absent from this task folder (only\n10|`SURVEY.md` + this plan exist). Hypothesis **(a) real double-hold is PROVEN**:\n11|a throwaway probe (`/tmp/kb-step1-probe.mjs`, not committed) claimed task-A\n12|and task-B as one `runnerId` and both holds are live; the existing\n13|`api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js` flow shows the dispatch path doing the\n14|same (runner `caps-1` direct-claims task A, then dispatch assigns it task B).\n15|The suspect widget is `PerRunnerTasksWidget` (one card per assignment, no\n16|per-runner grouping), so two holds for one `runnerId` render as two live\n17|\"Runner X\" cards — the reported look. `TaskCard` likewise badges every held\n18|task `RUNNING · <runnerId>`. Hypothesis (b) stale `running_*` labels remains\n19|possible as a secondary contributor; the backend fence + grouped UI below fix\n20|(a) and display-harden (b).\n21|\n22|## Goal\n23|\n24|Guarantee that one Runner executes at most one task at a time (protecting a\n25|memory-limited dev box from concurrent-work crashes), prove the guarantee with\n26|tests, and make the single-active-task state unmistakable in the UI.\n27|\n28|## Success Criteria\n29|\n30|1. A single `runnerId` can hold at most one live backend claim at any moment;\n31|   a second claim/dispatch attempt while one is live is refused loudly\n32|   (named error code, no silent queueing inside the Runner).\n33|2. The Runner daemon cannot start a second assignment while one is in flight,\n34|   even with a stale/retried dispatch answer.\n35|3. Every UI surface derives \"running\" from one source of truth, so two tasks\n36|   can never both render as running; stale `running_*` labels render as\n37|   stale/interrupted, never as live.\n38|4. Each Runner view shows exactly one \"current task\" slot plus an explicit\n39|   Busy/Free state (and, where cheap, queued-next and memory pressure).\n40|5. `npm run test:unit` passes; new regression tests cover the per-runner fence\n41|   and the UI single-active rendering.\n42|\n43|## Context and evidence (what research found)\n44|\n45|- Embedded engine already claims single-active execution: `ExecutionQueue`\n46|  serializes jobs (`api/flow/executionQueue.js`), and\n47|  `api/flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js` characterizes \"at most one live\n48|  running_* status\".\n49|- Frontend already has the right seam: `frontend/src/components/tasks/runningTask.js`\n50|  (`resolveRunningTask`, `isTaskRunning`, `isStaleRunner`) documents the\n51|  engine-owner lock and the \"phantom-second-runner\" bug class. Open question\n52|  is whether *all* surfaces use it (audit needed).\n53|- Fleet path has the gap: `ClaimStore.claim(taskId, runnerId, …)`\n54|  (`api/flow/claimStore.js`) enforces one holder per *task*, and dispatch\n55|  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, ~L993-1060) enforces a *fleet* cap and a\n56|  *per-project* cap — but nothing enforces one live hold per *runner*.\n57|  `countLiveHolds()` supports only a `projectId` filter; there is no\n58|  by-runner lookup. Two daemon processes sharing one `runnerId`/credential\n59|  (or a claim-route call racing a dispatch lease) can therefore hand one\n60|  Runner two live assignments on a small box.\n61|- Runner daemon loop (`runner/daemon.js`, `runDispatchLoop`) is sequentially\n62|  structured (poll → execute → poll), but there is no in-process\n63|  \"assignment in flight\" guard asserted around `executeAssignment`, and no\n64|  defense against a second process with the same identity.\n65|- Per-task live-claim UI exists: `RunnerBanner.jsx` renders from `task.claim`.\n66|  If two tasks ever carry claims for the same `runnerId` (see gap above), the\n67|  UI truthfully shows the forbidden state — the screenshot's \"one Runner, many\n68|  tasks\" look. Stale `running_*` labels are the second suspect (display-only).\n69|- Evidence gaps: the screenshot (`assets/18846.png`) is NOT present in this\n70|  task's docs folder (only `SURVEY.md` exists), and `SURVEY.md` has\n71|  `\"answers\": {}` (all questions unanswered). The plan below treats the survey\n72|  as open decisions with recommended defaults (§1), and Step 0 re-captures the\n73|  screenshot evidence.\n74|\n75|## How the survey shapes this plan (SURVEY.md, unanswered → advised defaults)\n76|\n77|| Survey Q | Options | Advised default used by this plan |\n78||---|---|---|\n79|| q1 — what to fix | real behavior / display / both / advise | **Both**: verify + fence real behavior first, then fix display (§5: backend fence precedes UI work) |\n80|| q2 — new tasks while busy | queue / reroute / manual move / advise | **Queue + reroute**: Runner refuses second assignment (`RUNNER_BUSY`); backend keeps the task claimable so another free Runner (or the same Runner when free) picks it up; no manual move needed for the common case |\n81|| q3 — what the screen shows (multi) | current task / Busy-Free / queue / memory warning | **All four**, in that priority order; memory warning is best-effort from heartbeat facts (`diskHeadroomMb`-style posture) and explicitly non-blocking |\n82|| q4 — ever allow >1 concurrent? | never / tiny background ok / if memory ok / advise | **Never** for task assignments; heartbeats/polling are the only concurrency (they are not tasks and must never render as tasks) |\n83|| q5 — what worried you in the screenshot | looked concurrent / stuck-doubled / other | Unanswered + screenshot missing → Step 0 reproduces both hypotheses (real double-hold vs stale-label display) before choosing which fix leads |\n84|\n85|If the human later answers the survey differently, only §5 Step 6 (queue /\n86|reroute policy text) and Step 7 (UI slots) need re-scoping; the per-runner\n87|fence (§5 Step 5) stands regardless.\n88|\n89|## Approach (make change easy, then make the change)\n90|\n91|Big research and structural work comes first; behavior changes land only after\n92|their seams and characterization tests exist:\n93|\n94|1. **Research first** (Steps 0–1): reproduce the two hypotheses with the\n95|   smallest possible probes; inventory every UI \"running\" signal.\n96|2. **Make change easy** (Steps 2–4): add the missing query seam\n97|   (holds-by-runner), characterization tests that pin current behavior, and a\n98|   UI audit routing every badge through `runningTask.js` — no behavior change.\n99|3. **Make the change** (Steps 5–7): backend per-runner fence, Runner-side\n100|   in-flight guard, UI single-slot clarity.\n101|4. **Assure it** (Steps 8–10): regression tests, docs, rollout/rollback.\n102|\n103|## Steps\n104|\n105|### Step 0 — Re-capture the evidence (research, first)\n106|\n107|- Re-obtain or re-create the `assets/18846.png` view: which page/widget showed\n108|  one Runner against several tasks? If the reporter can re-attach it, file it\n109|  under this task's `assets/`; otherwise reproduce via\n110|  `npm run capture:screenshot` against a fixture with two claim-carrying tasks\n111|  for the same `runnerId` (see Step 1 probe).\n112|- Decide which hypothesis the screenshot shows: (a) two live claims, one\n113|  `runnerId` (backend gap), or (b) one live claim + stale `running_*` labels\n114|  (display gap). Record the verdict at the top of this file before Step 5.\n115|- Validation: the recorded verdict names the page, the tasks, and which\n116|  hypothesis; a reviewer can re-open the same view.\n117|\n118|### Step 1 — Minimal reproduction probes (research, first)\n119|\n120|- Backend probe (throwaway, `/tmp`, not committed): drive `ClaimStore`\n121|  directly — claim task A as `runner-1`, then claim task B as `runner-1` —\n122|  and show both holds are live today. Then drive `POST /runners/dispatch`\n123|  twice for one `runnerId` with two claimable tasks and show whether two\n124|  leases are issued (mirror the style of\n125|  `api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`).\n126|- Frontend probe: render the suspect view with one engine-owner task plus a\n127|  second task carrying a stale `running_agent` label; note every element that\n128|  renders a live-looking RUNNING/claimed signal.\n129|- Validation: probes are independent of the later fix (they use public\n130|  routes/helpers); keep the backend probe's assertions to convert into the\n131|  Step 8 regression test.\n132|\n133|### Step 2 — Add the by-runner query seam (make change easy, no behavior change)\n134|\n135|- `api/flow/claimStore.js`: add `liveHoldsByRunner(runnerId)` (and optionally\n136|  extend `countLiveHolds({ runnerId })`), reusing the existing lazy-expiry\n137|  sweep in `_holding()`. Pure query — no call-site behavior changes.\n138|- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`: expose the data the UI needs — extend the\n139|  existing `liveAssignments` projection (~L468) or the runner-status payload\n140|  with `currentTaskId` / `liveHoldCount` per runner so the UI never joins\n141|  claims client-side.\n142|- Validation: `npm run test:api -- claimStore` passes; new unit tests assert\n143|  expiry-aware by-runner counts.\n144|\n145|### Step 3 — Characterization tests pinning current behavior (make change easy)\n146|\n147|- Add failing-or-pinning tests *before* the fence: \"second dispatch for a\n148|  busy runnerId is refused\" (expectation set to the DESIRED code, allowed to\n149|  fail until Step 5 — mark clearly as fence-pending), plus passing\n150|  characterization of today's fleet/project caps to prevent regressions.\n151|- Frontend: add a test rendering two claim/stale-running tasks for one runner\n152|  through the real view (not the helper in isolation) pinning today's\n153|  (wrong-looking) output, to flip in Step 7.\n154|- Validation: full `npm run test:unit` green except the explicitly-marked\n155|  fence-pending assertions.\n156|\n157|### Step 4 — UI signal audit + route every badge through the one helper (make change easy)\n158|\n159|- Inventory every \"running/live/claimed\" signal: `TaskCard`, `RunnerBanner`,\n160|  `ObservabilityDashboard`, `EngineStatePill`, `MobileMonitorView`,\n161|  `TaskDetailOverlay`, activity console — record which use\n162|  `resolveRunningTask`/`isTaskRunning`/`isStaleRunner` and which read raw\n163|  `task.status`/`task.claim`.\n164|- Convert stragglers to the helpers with NO visual redesign yet: stale labels\n165|  must already render as stale/interrupted after this step.\n166|- Validation: `npm run test:frontend` passes; the Step 1 frontend probe now\n167|  shows at most one live RUNNING badge.\n168|\n169|### Step 5 — Backend: one live hold per runner (make the change)\n170|\n171|- In `claim()`-issuing paths (`POST /runners/dispatch` candidate loop AND the\n172|  direct single-assignment claim route ~L846, AND the merge-lease path\n173|  ~L1067): refuse when the requesting `runnerId` already holds a live,\n174|  unexpired hold. Suggested contract: HTTP 409 + code `RUNNER_BUSY` with the\n175|  current `taskId`/`executionId` in the body (mirrors existing `CLAIM_CONFLICT`\n176|  / `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED` shapes).\n177|- Keep the refused task claimable (do NOT park it on the busy runner) so q2's\n178|  queue+reroute default holds: another free Runner can claim it; the busy\n179|  Runner's next poll after completing gets fresh work.\n180|- Decide + document TTL interplay: an expired hold must not block (lazy sweep\n181|  already handles this); a crashed Runner's hold blocks re-dispatch only until\n182|  TTL, same as today — no new resurrection logic.\n183|- Validation: fence-pending tests from Step 3 now pass; caps tests\n184|  (`runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`) and `singleActiveInvariant.test.js` still pass.\n185|\n186|### Step 6 — Runner daemon: in-flight guard + busy handling (make the change)\n187|\n188|- `runner/daemon.js`: assert a single-flight guard around `executeAssignment`\n189|  in `runDispatchLoop` (and the single-assignment path): never start a second\n190|  assignment while `state.executionId` is set; treat a second dispatch answer\n191|  arriving mid-run as a bug and back off rather than executing.\n192|- Handle `RUNNER_BUSY` like `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED`: log, back off\n193|  without consuming idle budget, re-poll (covers the two-processes-one-identity\n194|  case: the loser backs off instead of double-executing).\n195|- Optional hardening (only if Step 1 shows it is reachable): local pid/lockfile\n196|  so two daemons with the same `runnerId` on one box cannot both run; document\n197|  as defense-in-depth, not the primary fence (the backend fence is primary).\n198|- Validation: `runner/daemon.test.js` additions — busy answer backs off;\n199|  in-flight guard never double-executes (mirror the existing 429 test ~L1024).\n200|\n201|### Step 7 — UI: one unmistakable current-task slot per Runner (make the change)\n202|\n203|- Per Runner (settings/runners list + monitor): exactly one \"Current task\"\n204|  slot (task link + stage + elapsed), an explicit `BUSY`/`FREE` pill sourced\n205|  from the Step 2 payload (`liveHoldCount`/`currentTaskId`), a \"queued next\"\n206|  count when work is waiting, and a best-effort memory-pressure note from\n207|  heartbeat posture. Never render two live task rows under one Runner.\n208|- Keep `RunnerBanner` per task (it answers \"where is THIS task running\") but\n209|  ensure its copy cannot imply the Runner is otherwise free; link to the\n210|  Runner's single slot.\n211|- Validation: headless check via existing fixtures + `npm run capture:screenshot`\n212|  (no long-lived servers); flip the Step 3 frontend test to the new rendering.\n213|\n214|### Step 8 — Regression tests (assurance)\n215|\n216|- Backend: busy-runner dispatch refused (agent + merge + direct-claim paths);\n217|  refused task still claimable by a different runner; expired hold does not\n218|  block; two processes / double-poll with one identity cannot double-execute.\n219|- Frontend: one-runner-two-tasks fixture renders exactly one BUSY slot and one\n220|  live badge; stale labels render stale.\n221|- Runner: `RUNNER_BUSY` backoff; single-flight guard.\n222|- Gate: `npm run test:unit` fully green; run the touched suites\n223|  (`claimStore`, `runnerRoutes`, `runnerDispatchCaps`, `singleActiveInvariant`,\n224|  `daemon`, `runningTask`, dashboard) unmodified, no narrowing/deselect.\n225|\n226|### Step 9 — Documentation (assurance)\n227|\n228|- Update the Runner/operator docs: the one-task-per-Runner invariant, the\n229|  `RUNNER_BUSY` contract (code, status, retry-after behavior), queue+reroute\n230|  semantics, and what each UI slot means. Touch `agent-docs/` only where a\n231|  Runner invariant is already documented; otherwise the user-facing runner\n232|  settings/monitor help text + CHANGELOG-style note per repo convention.\n233|- Record the Step 0 verdict (screenshot hypothesis) and the survey-default\n234|  decisions (§1 table) in the task folder so a later human answer can be\n235|  diffed against what shipped.\n236|\n237|### Step 10 — Rollout + rollback (assurance)\n238|\n239|- Rollout is a normal deploy (backend fence + runner update + frontend);\n240|  backend first (old Runners treat 409 `RUNNER_BUSY` as a retryable dispatch\n241|  miss — verify this fallback in Step 6 tests so mixed versions are safe).\n242|- Rollback: revert backend fence → prior caps-only behavior; Each Runner view shows exactly one \"current task\" slot plus an explicit\n39|   Busy/Free state (and, where cheap, queued-next and memory pressure).\n40|5. `npm run test:unit` passes; new regression tests cover the per-runner fence\n41|   and the UI single-active rendering.\n42|\n43|## Context and evidence (what research found)\n44|\n45|- Embedded engine already claims single-active execution: `ExecutionQueue`\n46|  serializes jobs (`api/flow/executionQueue.js`), and\n47|  `api/flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js` characterizes \"at most one live\n48|  running_* status\".\n49|- Frontend already has the right seam: `frontend/src/components/tasks/runningTask.js`\n50|  (`resolveRunningTask`, `isTaskRunning`, `isStaleRunner`) documents the\n51|  engine-owner lock and the \"phantom-second-runner\" bug class. Open question\n52|  is whether *all* surfaces use it (audit needed).\n53|- Fleet path has the gap: `ClaimStore.claim(taskId, runnerId, …)`\n54|  (`api/flow/claimStore.js`) enforces one holder per *task*, and dispatch\n55|  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, ~L993-1060) enforces a *fleet* cap and a\n56|  *per-project* cap — but nothing enforces one live hold per *runner*.\n57|  `countLiveHolds()` supports only a `projectId` filter; there is no\n58|  by-runner lookup. Two daemon processes sharing one `runnerId`/credential\n59|  (or a claim-route call racing a dispatch lease) can therefore hand one\n60|  Runner two live assignments on a small box.\n61|- Runner daemon loop (`runner/daemon.js`, `runDispatchLoop`) is sequentially\n62|  structured (poll → execute → poll), but there is no in-process\n63|  \"assignment in flight\" guard asserted around `executeAssignment`, and no\n64|  defense against a second process with the same identity.\n65|- Per-task live-claim UI exists: `RunnerBanner.jsx` renders from `task.claim`.\n66|  If two tasks ever carry claims for the same `runnerId` (see gap above), the\n67|  UI truthfully shows the forbidden state — the screenshot's \"one Runner, many\n68|  tasks\" look. Stale `running_*` labels are the second suspect (display-only).\n69|- Evidence gaps: the screenshot (`assets/18846.png`) is NOT present in this\n70|  task's docs folder (only `SURVEY.md` exists), and `SURVEY.md` has\n71|  `\"answers\": {}` (all questions unanswered). The plan below treats the survey\n72|  as open decisions with recommended defaults (§1), and Step 0 re-captures the\n73|  screenshot evidence.\n74|\n75|## How the survey shapes this plan (SURVEY.md, unanswered → advised defaults)\n76|\n77|| Survey Q | Options | Advised default used by this plan |\n78||---|---|---|\n79|| q1 — what to fix | real behavior / display / both / advise | **Both**: verify + fence real behavior first, then fix display (§5: backend fence precedes UI work) |\n80|| q2 — new tasks while busy | queue / reroute / manual move / advise | **Queue + reroute**: Runner refuses second assignment (`RUNNER_BUSY`); backend keeps the task claimable so another free Runner (or the same Runner when free) picks it up; no manual move needed for the common case |\n81|| q3 — what the screen shows (multi) | current task / Busy-Free / queue / memory warning | **All four**, in that priority order; memory warning is best-effort from heartbeat facts (`diskHeadroomMb`-style posture) and explicitly non-blocking |\n82|| q4 — ever allow >1 concurrent? | never / tiny background ok / if memory ok / advise | **Never** for task assignments; heartbeats/polling are the only concurrency (they are not tasks and must never render as tasks) |\n83|| q5 — what worried you in the screenshot | looked concurrent / stuck-doubled / other | Unanswered + screenshot missing → Step 0 reproduces both hypotheses (real double-hold vs stale-label display) before choosing which fix leads |\n84|\n85|If the human later answers the survey differently, only §5 Step 6 (queue /\n86|reroute policy text) and Step 7 (UI slots) need re-scoping; the per-runner\n87|fence (§5 Step 5) stands regardless.\n88|\n89|## Approach (make change easy, then make the change)\n90|\n91|Big research and structural work comes first; behavior changes land only after\n92|their seams and characterization tests exist:\n93|\n94|1. **Research first** (Steps 0–1): reproduce the two hypotheses with the\n95|   smallest possible probes; inventory every UI \"running\" signal.\n96|2. **Make change easy** (Steps 2–4): add the missing query seam\n97|   (holds-by-runner), characterization tests that pin current behavior, and a\n98|   UI audit routing every badge through `runningTask.js` — no behavior change.\n99|3. **Make the change** (Steps 5–7): backend per-runner fence, Runner-side\n100|   in-flight guard, UI single-slot clarity.\n101|4. **Assure it** (Steps 8–10): regression tests, docs, rollout/rollback.\n102|\n103|## Steps\n104|\n105|### Step 0 — Re-capture the evidence (research, first)\n106|\n107|- Re-obtain or re-create the `assets/18846.png` view: which page/widget showed\n108|  one Runner against several tasks? If the reporter can re-attach it, file it\n109|  under this task's `assets/`; otherwise reproduce via\n110|  `npm run capture:screenshot` against a fixture with two claim-carrying tasks\n111|  for the same `runnerId` (see Step 1 probe).\n112|- Decide which hypothesis the screenshot shows: (a) two live claims, one\n113|  `runnerId` (backend gap), or (b) one live claim + stale `running_*` labels\n114|  (display gap). Record the verdict at the top of this file before Step 5.\n115|- Validation: the recorded verdict names the page, the tasks, and which\n116|  hypothesis; a reviewer can re-open the same view.\n117|\n118|### Step 1 — Minimal reproduction probes (research, first)\n119|\n120|- Backend probe (throwaway, `/tmp`, not committed): drive `ClaimStore`\n121|  directly — claim task A as `runner-1`, then claim task B as `runner-1` —\n122|  and show both holds are live today. Then drive `POST /runners/dispatch`\n123|  twice for one `runnerId` with two claimable tasks and show whether two\n124|  leases are issued (mirror the style of\n125|  `api/flow/runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`).\n126|- Frontend probe: render the suspect view with one engine-owner task plus a\n127|  second task carrying a stale `running_agent` label; note every element that\n128|  renders a live-looking RUNNING/claimed signal.\n129|- Validation: probes are independent of the later fix (they use public\n130|  routes/helpers); keep the backend probe's assertions to convert into the\n131|  Step 8 regression test.\n132|\n133|### Step 2 — Add the by-runner query seam (make change easy, no behavior change)\n134|\n135|- `api/flow/claimStore.js`: add `liveHoldsByRunner(runnerId)` (and optionally\n136|  extend `countLiveHolds({ runnerId })`), reusing the existing lazy-expiry\n137|  sweep in `_holding()`. Pure query — no call-site behavior changes.\n138|- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`: expose the data the UI needs — extend the\n139|  existing `liveAssignments` projection (~L468) or the runner-status payload\n140|  with `currentTaskId` / `liveHoldCount` per runner so the UI never joins\n141|  claims client-side.\n142|- Validation: `npm run test:api -- claimStore` passes; new unit tests assert\n143|  expiry-aware by-runner counts.\n144|\n145|### Step 3 — Characterization tests pinning current behavior (make change easy)\n146|\n147|- Add failing-or-pinning tests *before* the fence: \"second dispatch for a\n148|  busy runnerId is refused\" (expectation set to the DESIRED code, allowed to\n149|  fail until Step 5 — mark clearly as fence-pending), plus passing\n150|  characterization of today's fleet/project caps to prevent regressions.\n151|- Frontend: add a test rendering two claim/stale-running tasks for one runner\n152|  through the real view (not the helper in isolation) pinning today's\n153|  (wrong-looking) output, to flip in Step 7.\n154|- Validation: full `npm run test:unit` green except the explicitly-marked\n155|  fence-pending assertions.\n156|\n157|### Step 4 — UI signal audit + route every badge through the one helper (make change easy)\n158|\n159|- Inventory every \"running/live/claimed\" signal: `TaskCard`, `RunnerBanner`,\n160|  `ObservabilityDashboard`, `EngineStatePill`, `MobileMonitorView`,\n161|  `TaskDetailOverlay`, activity console — record which use\n162|  `resolveRunningTask`/`isTaskRunning`/`isStaleRunner` and which read raw\n163|  `task.status`/`task.claim`.\n164|- Convert stragglers to the helpers with NO visual redesign yet: stale labels\n165|  must already render as stale/interrupted after this step.\n166|- Validation: `npm run test:frontend` passes; the Step 1 frontend probe now\n167|  shows at most one live RUNNING badge.\n168|\n169|### Step 5 — Backend: one live hold per runner (make the change)\n170|\n171|- In `claim()`-issuing paths (`POST /runners/dispatch` candidate loop AND the\n172|  direct single-assignment claim route ~L846, AND the merge-lease path\n173|  ~L1067): refuse when the requesting `runnerId` already holds a live,\n174|  unexpired hold. Suggested contract: HTTP 409 + code `RUNNER_BUSY` with the\n175|  current `taskId`/`executionId` in the body (mirrors existing `CLAIM_CONFLICT`\n176|  / `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED` shapes).\n177|- Keep the refused task claimable (do NOT park it on the busy runner) so q2's\n178|  queue+reroute default holds: another free Runner can claim it; the busy\n179|  Runner's next poll after completing gets fresh work.\n180|- Decide + document TTL interplay: an expired hold must not block (lazy sweep\n181|  already handles this); a crashed Runner's hold blocks re-dispatch only until\n182|  TTL, same as today — no new resurrection logic.\n183|- Validation: fence-pending tests from Step 3 now pass; caps tests\n184|  (`runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`) and `singleActiveInvariant.test.js` still pass.\n185|\n186|### Step 6 — Runner daemon: in-flight guard + busy handling (make the change)\n187|\n188|- `runner/daemon.js`: assert a single-flight guard around `executeAssignment`\n189|  in `runDispatchLoop` (and the single-assignment path): never start a second\n190|  assignment while `state.executionId` is set; document\n197|  as defense-in-depth, not the primary fence (the backend fence is primary).\n198|- Validation: `runner/daemon.test.js` additions — busy answer backs off;\n199|  in-flight guard never double-executes (mirror the existing 429 test ~L1024).\n200|\n201|### Step 7 — UI: one unmistakable current-task slot per Runner (make the change)\n202|\n203|- Per Runner (settings/runners list + monitor): exactly one \"Current task\"\n204|  slot (task link + stage + elapsed), an explicit `BUSY`/`FREE` pill sourced\n205|  from the Step 2 payload (`liveHoldCount`/`currentTaskId`), a \"queued next\"\n206|  count when work is waiting, and a best-effort memory-pressure note from\n207|  heartbeat posture. Touch `agent-docs/` only where a\n231|  Runner invariant is already documented; otherwise the user-facing runner\n232|  settings/monitor help text + CHANGELOG-style note per repo convention.\n233|- Record the Step 0 verdict (screenshot hypothesis) and the survey-default\n234|  decisions (§1 table) in the task folder so a later human answer can be\n235|  diffed against what shipped.\n236|\n237|### Step 10 — Rollout + rollback (assurance)\n238|\n239|- Rollout is a normal deploy (backend fence + runner update + frontend);\n240|  backend first (old Runners treat 409 `RUNNER_BUSY` as a retryable dispatch\n241|  miss — verify this fallback in Step 6 tests so mixed versions are safe).\n242|- Rollback: revert backend fence → prior caps-only behavior; no data migration\n243|  (holds stay memory-only), so rollback is stateless.\n244|- Post-deploy check: fleet with ≥2 runners, ≥2 tasks — each runner shows\n245|  BUSY with exactly one current task; queue drains without overlap.\n246|\n247|## Risks / Open Questions\n248|\n249|- Screenshot missing + survey unanswered: Step 0 re-captures evidence; §1\n250|  defaults keep the plan executable either way.\n251|- Mixed-version fleet during rollout: old Runner receiving unknown 409 code\n252|  must back off, not crash — covered in Step 6.\n253|- TTL edge: a crashed Runner's hold still blocks ITS OWN identity until TTL;\n254|  acceptable (same as today's per-task behavior), documented in Step 9.\n255|- Out of scope: raising fleet/project caps, multi-task runners by config,\n256|  real memory-based admission control (memory UI is display-only).\n257|\n258|## Validation Plan (summary)\n259|\n260|| Step | Check |\n261||---|---|\n262|| 0–1 | Verdict recorded; mixed-version backoff verified; deploy/rollback noted |\n268|\n269|Highest-risk validation: Step 1's double-dispatch probe — if it shows the\n270|backend already refuses (hypothesis (a) wrong), Steps 5–6 shrink to hardening\n271|and the plan re-weights toward the Step 4/7 display fix.\n272|\n273|## Implementation notes (recorded by implementation stage, 2026-11-02)\n274|\n275|Contract as shipped:\n276|\n277|- `ClaimStore.claim()` fences one live hold per Runner (race-safe backstop;\n278|  synchronous with the insert). Same-task re-claim stays `CLAIM_CONFLICT`;\n279|  a second task answers `409 RUNNER_BUSY` with\n280|  `holder: { runnerId, taskId, executionId, epoch }`.\n281|- `POST /runners/dispatch` refuses a busy Runner with **`429 RUNNER_BUSY`**\n282|  (deviation from the plan's suggested 409: the daemon crashes on unknown\n283|  409 codes but backs off on any 429, so 429 is what keeps mixed-version\n284|  fleets safe per Step 10; it also matches the fleet-cap backpressure\n285|  family the daemon already handles). The in-loop claim sites map a raced\n286|  `RUNNER_BUSY` to the same 429 instead of continuing to later candidates.\n287|- `POST /tasks/:id/claim` answers `409 RUNNER_BUSY` via the store (conflict\n288|  family, mirrors `CLAIM_CONFLICT`).\n289|- Runner daemon: explicit `RUNNER_BUSY` branch (code-first, any status)\n290|  backs off without consuming idle budget; `tryEnterAssignment` /\n291|  `leaveAssignment` single-flight guard wraps `executeAssignment` in both\n292|  the dispatch loop and the single-assignment path. The `STALE_RUNNER`\n293|  heartbeat-then-retry path also backs off (no idle-budget burn, no crash)\n294|  when the retry itself is refused with `RUNNER_BUSY` / 429 / `RUNNER_PAUSED`\n295|  — e.g. a duplicate daemon sharing the identity — instead of letting the\n296|  refusal escape and kill the loop.
